programs.title: What we <s>run</s>
programs.intro: Two programmes so far: the Youth Climate Innovation Challenge for founders building solutions in informal settlements, and BeGreen Africa for young people running green waste businesses. Both sit under the five pillars below.

ycic.description: An incubator for youth-led green startups, from clean energy to waste tech, focused on solutions for informal settlements. Winners receive seed funding, six months of expert mentorship and a route to market.

begreen.description: A multi-partner green entrepreneurship programme for youth aged 18–35 in Kenya's waste management sector — 846 jobs created, ~USD 2.7M revenue generated, and 29.9M kgs of waste managed.

begreen.title: BeGreen Africa <g>Initiative</g>
begreen.intro: A multi-partner programme building green entrepreneurship in waste management — simultaneously addressing youth unemployment and environmental degradation.
begreen.about1: The BeGreen Africa Initiative is a multi-partner programme implemented in Kenya by UNICEF/Generation Unlimited, the Tony Elumelu Foundation, and the IKEA Foundation, with incubation support from STEM Impact Center Kenya.
begreen.about2: It targets youth aged 18–35 years to build green entrepreneurship in the waste management sector — simultaneously addressing youth unemployment and environmental degradation.
begreen.about3: The programme aligns with Kenya Vision 2030, the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), and national commitments under the Paris Agreement and multiple SDGs.

focus.title: Plastic Waste Management
focus.desc: Youth enterprises processing and recycling plastic waste across urban and rural Kenya.

focus.title: Organic Waste & Biogas
focus.desc: Converting organic waste into biogas and compost, creating circular economy value chains.

focus.title: E-Waste Enterprises
focus.desc: Highest-earning sub-sector — responsible collection and processing of electronic waste.

focus.title: Waste-to-Value Innovation
focus.desc: Transforming waste streams into marketable products, creating jobs and reducing landfill pressure.

outcomes.title: Employment Creation
items: 846 total jobs created — far exceeding the 260 projected
Average 8.1 jobs per enterprise vs. 2.6 benchmark
Mentored enterprises created 531 jobs vs. 104 without mentorship

outcomes.title: Revenue Generation
items: ~7x revenue growth from Nov 2023 to Jul 2025
Avg monthly revenue grew from KShs 81K to KShs 203K

outcomes.title: Environmental Impact
items: 29.9 million kgs of waste managed total
11.6M kgs plastic + 18.4M kgs organic waste diverted
Incubated enterprises managed 27.9M kgs vs. 76K without
Significant contribution to Kenya's circular economy

begreen.inclusionBody: Between 74% and 90% of all participants were classified as marginalized — demonstrating the programme's strong inclusion focus. Even among funded youth, marginalization rates ranged from 74.3% to 82.4%.
begreen.conclusion1: The BeGreen Africa Kenya Initiative has significantly exceeded its core targets across all three programme pillars: employment creation (846 jobs vs. 260 projected), revenue generation (~USD 2.7M annually vs. USD 1M target), and waste management (29.9M kgs diverted).
begreen.conclusion2: As Kenya advances its climate goals, the BeGreen experience affirms that youth are not only beneficiaries but architects of sustainable development.

quiz.title: Climate Readiness Quiz
quiz.subtitle: Test your climate knowledge — earn your badge
quiz.introBody: 8 questions covering Kenya's climate policy, renewable energy, carbon markets, and global climate action. Takes about 3 minutes.

questions.question: What percentage of Kenya's electricity comes from renewable sources?
questions.explanation: Kenya is a renewable energy leader! About 92% of its electricity comes from geothermal, hydro, wind and solar — one of the highest rates in Africa.

questions.question: What does 'GCF' stand for in climate finance?
questions.explanation: The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is the world's largest dedicated climate fund, helping developing countries like Kenya respond to climate change.

questions.question: Which renewable energy source generates the MOST electricity in Kenya?
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy from the Great Rift Valley generates about 47% of Kenya's electricity. Kenya is the 8th largest geothermal producer in the world!

questions.question: What is Kenya's NDC target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 2030?
questions.explanation: Kenya's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) commits to a 32% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030, conditional on international support.

questions.question: Which Kenyan county is MOST vulnerable to drought and climate stress?
questions.explanation: Turkana County in northern Kenya is one of the most climate-vulnerable areas in Africa, facing severe droughts, food insecurity, and water scarcity.

questions.question: What does 'UNFCCC' stand for?
options: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
UN Fund for Climate Change Control
UN Finance Committee on Climate Change
UN Forum for Carbon Credit Control
questions.explanation: The UNFCCC (UN Framework Convention on Climate Change) is the international treaty that guides global climate action, including the Paris Agreement.

questions.question: What is a 'carbon credit'?
options: A permit to emit 1 tonne of CO₂
questions.explanation: A carbon credit represents the right to emit 1 tonne of CO₂. Companies can buy credits to offset their emissions or earn them by reducing emissions.

questions.question: What is the Paris Agreement's goal for limiting global temperature rise?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement aims to limit global warming to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels. Every fraction of a degree matters for communities like those in Kenya!
